mentl/899154c:
Before: when the user wrote `let xs = [1,2,3]` at top level and ANY
function in prelude/runtime took `xs` as a parameter (every collection
primitive does: map, filter, fold, take, drop, ...), the lowerer's
capture detector asked is_global("xs"), got true because of the user's
let, and filtered xs out of the capture list. The inner function's
body kept LGlobal("xs") which the emitter turned into global.get $xs —
the USER's top-level binding, not the enclosing function's parameter.

Effect on user code:

  fn dbl(x) = x * 2
  fn add(a, b) = a + b
  let xs = [1, 2, 3]
  let ys = map(dbl, xs)          -- ys = [2, 4, 6] (fine)
  println(to_string(fold(ys, 0, add)))   -- prints 6, expected 12

Because inside fold's handler, iterate's go_0 was reading global $xs
(= [1, 2, 3]) instead of iterate's parameter (= ys = [2, 4, 6]). So
fold was silently folding the original user list, not the mapped one.

Fix: filter_real_captures now takes env. When the most-recent env
binding for a free var is Declared("param") — i.e., a parameter of an
enclosing function — the name is KEPT in captures regardless of
whether it appears in top_globals. Env's most-recent lookup already
implements lexical scoping; we just weren't consulting it.

Covered patterns:
  - fn inner capturing enclosing fn's param that shadows top-level let
  - recursive inner fn capturing enclosing param with same name as global
  - fold/map/filter chains where the user's top-level list name
    collided with a collection-primitive's xs parameter

Not yet covered (follow-up): inner `let x = ...` inside a function
body that shadows a top-level `let x`. Both bindings have the same
Inferred("let") reason in env so they can't be distinguished by
reason alone — needs either position tracking or a separate "local"
marker for inner lets.

Tool: lower_print.lux now shows closure captures as `|[name1, name2]|`
immediately after the function signature. A function that should be
capturing something but shows empty captures is visibl

celezdial/89e3feb:
The context forced sampleRate 44100 while Android hardware runs 48000.
An off-rate context makes Chrome insert a resampler and drops the
stream off the fast audio path (AAudio), adding jitter and callback
overruns. Phones tolerated that tax while the Freeverb was dangling
and unrendered; once the reverb fix put ~50 comb-filter nodes into the
live graph, mid-range Androids went over the edge and glitched.

TUNING.sampleRate becomes null, meaning hardware rate; the engine only
pins a rate when a tuning profile asks (the lo-fi presets keep their
16kHz character). Pitch is computed in Hz throughout, so nothing else
changes. The footer drops its 44.1kHz claim.

The damp sweep tick relaxes from 20Hz to 10Hz — still five steps per
cycle with the MOD knob pinned at its 2Hz max, half the cross-thread
filter-param writes (each tick touches 8 comb filters).

The "now" button now syncs the city picker: after geolocation it
reverse-geocodes the fix and fills the field with the real place name
instead of the "here" placeholder.
